claim_ledger.status: Supported conditional counting argument and pinned-source counterexample
claim_ledger.safe_wording: Exact-text duplicate suppression can inherit a bounded retrieval window when only retrieved records supply its existing-hash set.
claim_ledger.exact_statement: Let N distinct already-stored fact hashes be eligible for redelivery, and let U be the distinct existing hashes presented to admission. Under the tested same-scope sequential ADD path, if every fact outside U is re-emitted once and no other filter rejects it, N-|U| repeated records survive. Since |U|<=k, this is at least max(0,N-k).
conditions: Distinct exact-text hashes, fixed scope, already stored facts and sequential delivery
Re-emission assumption must be explicit; arbitrary natural model outputs need not satisfy it
The exact N-|U| statement is about the specified admission path, not all memory APIs
false_or_overgeneralizing: Mem0 necessarily inserts N-k duplicates on every retry.
Every store larger than k must duplicate facts.
MD5 is globally broken.
The elementary counting bound is a new recovery theorem.
The vendor promised request exactly-once semantics.

claim_ledger.safe_wording: A 96-cell controlled-extraction sweep through the pinned Mem0 OSS path separates exact fact content from physical multiplicity, with hash and real BGE embedding factors and two authored interventions.
conditions: 96 parameterized executions, not 96 independent model trials
Widened candidate and exact-admission arms are authored sequential controls
The fact-set check is exact literal equality in authored fixtures
false_or_overgeneralizing: Controls are production-ready concurrent deduplication fixes.

The sweep estimates production incidence.

claim_ledger.safe_wording: The post hoc retrieval probe queries all 84 baseline literal facts in four frozen states at budgets 5, 10 and 20, producing 1008 registered search cells. All exact queried strings remain present. Native retry stores can return fewer distinct literal strings despite this preserved target presence.
conditions: Protocol frozen before searches, but designed after duplicate writes were observed
Only selected fresh-context stores, all baseline facts, identical native BGE+BM25 reader, threshold zero and native optional-spaCy fallback
Exact stored text is the query: this is a literal exposure probe, not a semantic QA benchmark
Additional record identities/timestamps are part of the observed duplicate-bearing state; multiplicity alone is not separately manipulated while all metadata is held fixed
Queries and budgets are dependent; no confidence interval or natural-workload rate follows
false_or_overgeneralizing: Recall or answer quality fell in 213 queries.
Duplicate slots always displace distinct context.
All 213 duplicate-bearing cells have lower literal diversity.
The probe demonstrates agent harm, semantic diversity loss or measured token waste.

claim_ledger.safe_wording: At the pinned MemTX commit, the tested old transactions retrieve a post-begin record absent from their captured snapshots; two empty-snapshot authority variants supersede a post-begin rival where nonempty-snapshot controls reject it temporally. These disagree with the paper snapshot-read and pre-authority rejection descriptions in the tested boundaries.
conditions: Eight read cases, eight old-writer cases and eight fresh-writer controls; no arbitrary state-space theorem
Fresh-transaction correction is intended and the paper itself discusses retry escaping transaction-local temporal protection
The paper explicitly permits partial commit; arbitrary multi-record predicate serializability is not the tested contract
94 original core unit tests pass; optional full-suite tau2 collection failure remains disclosed

Passing the source tests establishes complete conformance.
